items.stem: An executive asks the assistant a question and it returns finance documents they should not see. What control prevents this?

options.text: Document-level access control enforced at query time
options.rationale: Correct: document-level access trims results to what the user is authorised to see, even when they ask.

options.text: A longer system prompt asking the model to be careful
options.rationale: Prompt wording does not reliably enforce authorisation on retrieved documents.
Performance tiers do not enforce access.

items.explanation: Correct: document-level access trims results to what the user is authorised to see, even when they ask.

items.stem: Which TWO are reasons to use hybrid search in Azure AI Search? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Exact terms and identifiers must match precisely
options.rationale: Correct: keyword matching captures exact codes that vectors may miss.

options.text: Semantic paraphrases of a question must also match
options.rationale: Correct: vector search captures meaning beyond exact wording.

options.text: You want to return every document in full
options.rationale: RAG needs concise, relevant results, not full dumps.

options.text: You want to remove access controls
options.rationale: Access control is unrelated to the hybrid-search rationale.

items.explanation: Correct: keyword matching captures exact codes that vectors may miss.

items.stem: Microsoft's guidance for Azure AI Search connecting to an Azure OpenAI embedding model with public access disabled is to:

options.text: Use the search service's managed identity as a trusted service
options.rationale: Correct: managed identity plus trusted-service access lets the services connect without public access or shared keys.
That defeats the network isolation goal.

options.text: Share an API key in the index definition
options.rationale: Embedding keys in definitions is the pattern managed identity replaces.
